subject: Information Theory
title: The Nyquist Sampling Theorem
description: A quick, practical guide to The Nyquist Sampling Theorem.

hook.text: CD audio samples sound 44,100 times per second. That specific number isn't arbitrary—it's the minimum required.

buildup.text: Nyquist proved: to perfectly capture a signal, sample at least twice its highest frequency.

discovery.text: Human hearing tops out at about 20 kHz. Twice that is 40 kHz. CDs use 44.1 kHz to add a safety margin.

twist.text: Sample below the Nyquist rate and you get aliasing: phantom frequencies that weren't in the original signal.

climax.text: This theorem bridges analog and digital. It guarantees perfect reconstruction from enough discrete samples.

punchline.text: Sample fast enough and nothing is lost.

quiz.question: What does the Nyquist theorem require?
options: Sample at least twice the highest frequency
